title: Clifford-hierarchy stabilizer formalism with applications to twisted quantum doubles
authors: Christopher Fechisin, Kieran Cooney, Mathi Raja, Victor V. Albert, Dominic J. Williamson, Kyle Kawagoe, Seth Musser
abstract: Recent work has shown that quantum double models can be used to circumvent the Bravyi-Koenig bound. In particular, this is achieved through code-switching protocols in which non-Pauli stabilizer phases appear as intermediate codes. We introduce the $X\mathcal C^{(k)}_d$ stabilizer formalism, which generalizes the Pauli stabilizer formalism by combining Pauli-$X$ operators with diagonal operators drawn from a fixed level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy on prime-dimensional qudits. This yields a natural class of beyond-Pauli stabilizer models, including many twisted quantum double phases. We classify a large class of these $X\mathcal C^{(k)}_d$ stabilizer states, showing that they are uniform superpositions over affine-linear subspaces with diagonal phases. In particular, when the stabilizers of a state require operators from level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy, we show that the diagonal gates required to produce the phases in the wavefunction sit one level higher. We further show that every 2D twisted quantum double ${\cal D}^ω(\mathbb{Z}_p^n)$ with $ω$ a product of type-III cocycles and $p$ an odd prime admits a realization using only Clifford ($k=2$) stabilizers, and we conjecture that phases where $ω$ contains a type-I or type-II cocycle require level-$p$ Clifford-hierarchy stabilizers for $p$-dimensional qudits. Finally, we demonstrate that a pair of qudit toric codes may be deterministically prepared in a logical magic state by measuring $X\mathcal C^{(k)}_d$ stabilizers. Together, these results provide a concrete stabilizer framework for topological codes beyond Pauli stabilizer models and their logical gates.
summary: This paper introduces the $X\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_d$ stabilizer formalism to analyze topological quantum codes beyond the standard Pauli model, specifically targeting Twisted Quantum Double (TQD) phases. The authors classify these states and determine the minimum stabilizer level required to realize complex topological orders. This provides a concrete, generalized framework for building and understanding topological quantum memory and gates.
main_problem: The paper develops a generalized stabilizer formalism to analyze topological quantum codes beyond the standard Pauli stabilizer model, specifically addressing twisted quantum double (TQD) phases.
main_result: It establishes the $X\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_d$ stabilizer formalism, showing that many TQD phases can be realized using Clifford stabilizers, and providing a concrete framework for topological codes beyond Pauli stabilizers.
method: The authors use group theory, Clifford hierarchy analysis, and stabilizer formalism to classify states and determine the minimal stabilizer level required to encode specific topological orders.
model_or_system: The focus is on Clifford-hierarchy stabilizer models, which generalize Pauli stabilizers by incorporating diagonal operators from higher levels of the Clifford hierarchy on prime-dimensional qudits. These models are applied to study Twisted Quantum Double (TQD) phases, which host non-abelian anyons.
key_observables: The minimal level $k$ of the stabilizer code, the structure of the 3-cocycle $\omega$, and the resulting topological order (e.g., $2D$ TQD $D_{\omega}(\mathbb{Z}_n^p)$).
important_parameters: The prime dimension $p$ of the qudits, the level $k$ of the Clifford hierarchy, and the structure of the cocycle $\omega$ (Type-I, Type-II, Type-III).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the equivalence between certain quantum doubles $D(G)$ and $D_{\omega}(A)$ when $G$ is nil-2, and conjectures regarding the required stabilizer level for specific cocycle types.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometry of TQD stabilizers, the algorithm for computing the 3-cocycle $\omega|f$ on a face, and the action of logical operators on the codespace.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the generalized $X\mathcal{C}^{(k)}_d$ formalism, then applying it to characterize TQD models by relating the required stabilizer level $k$ to the cocycle structure $\omega$, and finally drawing connections to the algebraic structure of the underlying quantum double groups $D(G)$.
why_interesting: This work provides a deep mathematical link between abstract group theory (quantum doubles) and the physical realization of topological quantum error-correcting codes, which is central to fault-tolerant quantum computation.
